interpretations: Count distinct orders with at least one matching risk/margin record by `ordertune`; average those counts across types with matches; return one row with the mean count for types above that average and their mean excess over it.

Count distinct orders with at least one matching risk/margin record by `ordertune`; include defined types with zero matches in the overall average; return one row with the mean count for types above that average and their mean excess over it.

Count joined risk/margin–order rows by `ordertune`, so an order with multiple risk/margin records contributes multiple times; average those counts across types with matches; return one row with the mean count for types above that average and their mean excess over it.

Count joined risk/margin–order rows by `ordertune`; include defined types with zero matches in the overall average; return one row with the mean count for types above that average and their mean excess over it.
For any of these counts, return the per-type counts as well as the single summary row.
For any of these counts, treat a null `ordertune` as its own type when calculating the overall average and selecting types above it.
Exclude orders with a null `ordertune` from the per-type counts and averages.
Include types present in `orders` with zero risk/margin matches in the overall average, but exclude defined types absent from `orders`.
queries:
WITH type_counts AS (
  SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(DISTINCT o.recordvault) AS order_count
  FROM orders AS o
  JOIN riskandmargin AS r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault
  GROUP BY o.ordertune
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(order_count) AS average_count
  FROM type_counts
)
SELECT
  AVG(t.order_count) AS mean_count,
  AVG(t.order_count - a.average_count) AS mean_excess
FROM type_counts AS t
CROSS JOIN overall AS a
WHERE t.order_count > a.average_count

WITH order_types(ordertune) AS (
  VALUES ('Stop'), ('Market'), ('Limit'), ('StopLimit')
),
type_counts AS (
  SELECT t.ordertune,
         COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN r.riskandmarginpivot IS NOT NULL THEN o.orderspivot END) AS order_count
  FROM order_types AS t
  LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.ordertune = t.ordertune
  LEFT JOIN riskandmargin AS r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault
  GROUP BY t.ordertune
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(order_count) AS avg_count
  FROM type_counts
)
SELECT AVG(tc.order_count) AS mean_count,
       AVG(tc.order_count - ov.avg_count) AS mean_excess
FROM type_counts AS tc
CROSS JOIN overall AS ov
WHERE tc.order_count > ov.avg_count

WITH counts AS (
  SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(*) AS match_count
  FROM riskandmargin AS r
  JOIN orders AS o ON o.recordvault = r.ordervault
  GROUP BY o.ordertune
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(match_count) AS avg_count
  FROM counts
)
SELECT
  AVG(c.match_count) AS mean_count,
  AVG(c.match_count - a.avg_count) AS mean_excess
FROM counts AS c
CROSS JOIN overall AS a
WHERE c.match_count > a.avg_count

WITH order_types(ordertune) AS (
  VALUES ('Stop'), ('Market'), ('Limit'), ('StopLimit')
),
type_counts AS (
  SELECT t.ordertune, COUNT(r.riskandmarginpivot) AS row_count
  FROM order_types AS t
  LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.ordertune = t.ordertune
  LEFT JOIN riskandmargin AS r ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault
  GROUP BY t.ordertune
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(row_count) AS mean_count
  FROM type_counts
)
SELECT
  AVG(c.row_count) AS mean_count_above_average,
  AVG(c.row_count - a.mean_count) AS mean_excess
FROM type_counts AS c
CROSS JOIN overall AS a
WHERE c.row_count > a.mean_count

WITH type_counts AS (
  SELECT ordertune, COUNT(*) AS order_count
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY ordertune
)
SELECT ordertune, order_count
FROM type_counts
WHERE order_count > (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM type_counts)
